# Search UX design: query input, zero-results states, and result presentation

Curated by Skill Harbor — @owl-listener's search-UX skill: design the full retrieval experience — forgiving entry (descriptive placeholders, width signaling query length, autofocus, Enter-to-submit, clear/reset, completions after 2-3 characters with recents → trending → predicted, 5-8 suggestions max per Hick's Law, keyboard navigation, query-term highlighting) — search-as-navigation (navigational destinations in suggestions, exact-match pages first, never "no results" for destinations that exist), results presentation (list vs grid vs grouped-by-type, result counts, matched-field signaling, decision-enough snippets), ranking (recency, popularity, exact-title match, personalization with surfaced sort logic), faceted refinement (context-relevant filters with counts, individually removable, clear-all), the zero-results state treated as a retention moment (confirm the query, typo corrections, broader terms, browse/support alternatives — never a blank page), and search analytics (top queries, zero-result queries, refinement rate, click position, abandonment). Honest caveats: methodology only — it doesn't implement the search backend, only its UX; keep it on mobile too (search is often primary navigation there). MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
